chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “What do you think about the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, ‘What becomes unlawful through breastfeeding is what becomes unlawful through lineage’? Explain it to me.”

He said: “Every woman who suckles, from the milk of her husband, the child of another woman, whether a girl or a boy, then that is the breastfeeding about which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله spoke. And every woman who suckles, from the milk of two husbands that she had, one after another, a girl or a boy, then that is a breastfeeding that is not the breastfeeding about which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said, ‘What becomes unlawful through breastfeeding is what becomes unlawful through lineage.’”

key_terms.الرَّضَاعِ: breastfeeding that establishes a legal milk-kinship relationship
key_terms.النَّسَبِ: lineage-based blood relationship that carries marriage prohibitions
key_terms.فَحْلَيْنِ: two different husbands, indicating two separate milk attributions
key_terms.فَحْلِهَا: her husband, to whom the milk is legally attributed in this ruling
key_terms.لَبَنِ: the milk through which the breastfeeding relationship is formed

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith “What is unlawful through breastfeeding is unlawful through lineage” mean in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal meaning of the Prophetic statement that certain kinship prohibitions are established through breastfeeding just as they are through lineage. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام clarifies that the effective breastfeeding relation is tied to milk attributed to one husband, while nursing connected to two different husbands does not fall under that same ruling.
